2607.08362.title: Echoes Across Vietnam's Highlands, Delta, and Coast: A Multilingual Corpus for Cham, Khmer, and Tay-Nung
2607.08362.paper_summary: Vietnam's ethnic minority languages are almost absent from the field of Natural Language Processing (NLP), and the challenge goes beyond data scarcity: Cham, Khmer, and Tay-Nung differ sharply in script, Vietnamese contact, and standardization, conditions under which standard multilingual adaptation can learn the wrong signals. We introduce CKTN, the first corpus and benchmark for these languages (44,367 documents, 24M subword tokens), spanning continued pretraining, category classification, and summary-document retrieval. We show that existing multilingual encoders severely fragment these languages, and that common adaptation metrics can mislead: models may lower language-modeling loss or excel at lexical-overlap retrieval while still failing at semantic generalization across documents. We address this with a script-aware adaptation recipe - vocabulary augmentation combined with calibrated replaced-token pretraining - that prevents the discriminator from exploiting trivial script mismatches. The result is an encoder with substantially less fragmentation and the strongest classification performance among evaluated models, exposing the limits of lexical-overlap retrieval as an evaluation signal.
2607.08362.paper_summary_zh: 越南的少數民族語言在自然語言處理（NLP）領域幾乎不存在，而挑戰不僅僅是數據稀缺：占族語、柬埔寨語和泰農語在字母、越南語接觸和標準化方面差異明顯，在這些條件下，標準的多語言適應可能會學習到錯誤的信號。<lb/>我們介紹了CKTN，這是這些語言的第一個語料庫和基準（44,367份文檔，24M子詞標記），涵蓋了持續的預訓練、類別分類和摘要文檔檢索。<lb/>我們顯示現有的多語言編碼器嚴重碎片化這些語言，並且常見的適應指標可能會誤導：模型可能會降低語言建模損失或在詞彙重疊檢索方面表現出色，但在文檔之間的語義泛化上仍然失敗。<lb/>我們通過一種考慮字母的適應方案來解決這個問題——詞彙增強結合校準的替換標記預訓練——這可以防止鑑別器利用微不足道的字母不匹配。<lb/>結果是一個碎片化程度大大降低的編碼器，並且在評估的模型中具有最強的分類性能，揭示了詞彙重疊檢索作為評估信號的局限性。
